L0: # How products and prices work
L1: 
L2: Learn how products and prices in Stripe model your business.
L3: 
L4: Read this page in your terminal: [install the Stripe CLI](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/install) (v1.43.3+) and run `stripe docs`. [Reference](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/docs)
L5: ## Start here: Integrate with Stripe using skills and plugins
L6: 
L7: Stripe provides skills and plugins for agents to build faster and more accurately. See [Agent skills](https://docs.stripe.com/skills.md) for more information.
L8: 
L9: **Quickstart**: Install the Stripe CLI with `npm install -g @stripe/cli` and run `stripe agent setup`.
L10: Products and prices are core resources for many Stripe integrations. Products define what your business offers, whether that’s goods or services. Prices define how much and how often to charge for products.
L11: You can create products and prices in Stripe or [import](https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/manage-prices.md#import-products-prices) them into Stripe through the [API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/products.md).
L12: After you create products and prices, you can use them with [Checkout Sessions](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md), [Payment Links](https://docs.stripe.com/payment-links.md), [Invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/invoicing.md), [Quotes](https://docs.stripe.com/quotes/create.md), or a custom integration to create [Subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing.md).
L13: ## Products
L14: 
L15: Products describe the specific goods or services you offer to your customers. Use cases include:
L16: 
L17: - **E-commerce**: If you sell clothes online, you can create a separate product for each size and color combination of shirts, for example.
L18: - **SaaS platform**: You could offer basic and premium pricing tiers, where basic and premium are separate products.
L19: - **Donation platform**: You accept donations for several different causes, and each cause is a different product.
L20: ### Product IDs
L21: 
L22: Each product has a unique ID. Unlike most Stripe resources, you can choose the ID of the product yourself. We recommend choosing an ID that makes it easy to integrate Stripe with other systems you use. For example, if you’re selling physical goods, you can use the internal ID from your own systems.
L23: ### Product names
L24: 
L25: When you create a product in Stripe, you have to provide a name. You can optionally add other attributes, like a description or image. If you’re using [Stripe Tax](https://docs.stripe.com/tax.md), you can also define a [tax code](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/tax-codes.md) for each product, such as pet grooming, e-books, or SaaS. Stripe Tax uses the tax code to automatically calculate and collect sales taxes during purchase.
L26: ## Prices
L27: 
L28: In Stripe, prices include additional information, such as tax behavior, volume tiers, and recurrence intervals for subscriptions. You don’t need to create new prices for each purchase–if you’re selling a product for one price, you only need to create one price. You can also make this price the [default price](https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/manage-prices.md#default-price) for the product.
L29: ### One-time and recurring payments
L30: 
L31: Prices can either be one-time or recurring. Subscriptions use recurring prices to charge the customer at an interval, such as “once a month.” If you sell the same service at several different intervals, it’s best to create multiple recurring prices for the same product. Learn more about [pricing models](https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/pricing-models.md#flat-rate).
L32: ### Variable pricing
L33: 
L34: You can use two types of variable pricing:
L35: 
L36: - **Inline pricing**: You define the price for your customer when you create a subscription, invoice, Checkout Session, or Payment Link.
L37: - **Pay-what-you-want pricing**: The customer fills in the price they pay, such as with a tip or donation. Recurring payments don’t support this type of variable pricing. See how to [let customers decide what to pay](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/pay-what-you-want.md) for single payments.
L38: #### Inline pricing
L39: 
L40: In some cases, you might want to use a custom price that hasn’t been preconfigured. For example, you might want to use inline prices when you manage your product catalog outside of Stripe. You can only create inline prices through the API.
L41: ### Multiple currencies
L42: A single Price can support multiple currencies. This helps you manage localized pricing when selling internationally. For example, if you sell a product in the US for 10 USD, in Europe for 9 EUR, and in Japan for 1300 JPY, the same `Price` object can cover all three currencies. Each purchase uses one of the supported currencies for the price, depending on how you use the price in your integration.
L43: Learn more about [multi-currency prices](https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/manage-prices.md#create-multi-currency-prices).
L44: > If you [create invoice items](https://docs.stripe.com/api/invoiceitems/create.md) or charges with the API, Stripe processes the amount and currency you explicitly provide. The localized price isn’t automatically calculated, and you’re responsible for passing the correct amount and currency for your customer’s region. We recommend using the [pricing.price](https://docs.stripe.com/api/invoiceitems/create.md#create_invoiceitem-pricing-price) parameter to pass the price ID.
L45: ### Multiple prices
L46: 
L47: Products can use multiple prices to define different pricing options. The prices share the product description, and it looks the same on the customer’s receipt and invoice—only the pricing differs. Because a product can have multiple prices associated with it, you need to specify which price to use when creating Checkout Sessions, Payment Links, invoices, quotes, or subscriptions.
L48: ### Unit amount
L49: 
L50: Most prices define a fixed `unit_amount`, but you can also configure the price to function with different tiers or usage-based models. Learn more about [tiered pricing](https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/pricing-models.md#tiered-pricing) and [usage-based pricing](https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/pricing-models.md#usage-based-pricing).
L51: ### Tax behavior
L52: 
L53: If you use Stripe Tax, you can specify the `tax_behavior` for the price to determine whether the tax is already included in the amount, or if it needs to be added. Learn more about [tax behavior](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/products-prices-tax-codes-tax-behavior.md#tax-behavior).
L54: ## Model your product catalog
L55: 
L56: Create a separate product for each distinct option a customer chooses between. Use prices for billing variants (interval, currency) of the same product.
L57: 
L58: > If two options appear as different rows on your pricing page, they must be different products. If they’re the same row billed at a different interval (monthly versus annual), they’re different prices on one product.
L59: ### Example: SaaS with multiple tiers
L60: 
L61: A business with Starter, Professional, and Enterprise plans where they’re each available monthly and annually, need to create:
L62: 
L63: - **3 products**: Starter, Professional, Enterprise
L64: - **2 prices per product**: Monthly, Annual
L65: Checkout, Payment Links, and invoices display the **Product name** for each line item. With distinct products per tier, each option shows its tier name. With one product and many prices, all options display the same product name. Customers can’t distinguish tiers.
L66: 
L67: > Don’t attach prices for different tiers to a single product. Line items that share a product share its name and description on receipts and invoices. This means only the amount differs.
L68: ### When to create a new product
L69: 
L70: - Distinct name on your pricing page (for example, “Basic” versus “Pro”)
L71: - Different features or entitlements
L72: - Different [tax code](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/tax-codes.md)
L73: - Needs to appear as a separate line item
L74: ### When to add a price to an existing product
L75: 
L76: - Same plan, different billing interval (monthly / annual)
L77: - Same plan, different currency
L78: - Price change (create new price, [archive](https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/manage-prices.md#archive-price) old one)
L79: 
L80: ## Working with products and prices
L81: ### Create or import products and prices
L82: 
L83: The quickest way to get started with products and prices is to create them through the [Stripe Dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/products).
L84: If you have a large product catalog that you manage using a spreadsheet or other software, you might prefer to import the product catalog programmatically using the [Products](https://docs.stripe.com/api/products.md) and [Prices](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices.md) API. Learn more about [import products and prices](https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/manage-prices.md#import-products-prices).
L85: If you need to charge an amount of money that’s different for each transaction (for example, a user-selected donation amount), you can create the product, but not create a price. Instead, you can use the `price_data` parameter when creating Checkout Sessions, Payment Links, or Subscriptions to set the particular price.
L86: This method generates `Price` and `Product` objects that are relevant for the specific Checkout Session, Payment Link, or Subscription. While the `Price` objects are temporary and not visible in the Dashboard, the associated `Product` objects aren’t always temporary. For example, `Price` objects created with `price_data` don’t appear in product searches or lists in the Dashboard.
L87: You can still view these objects directly by constructing a specific URL in the Dashboard, but they won’t show up in the main catalog.
L88: ### Use products and prices
L89: 
L90: #### Stripe Checkout
L91: 
L92: When creating a Checkout Session, specify the price `id` for each line item. The Checkout Session uses the price to compute the order total. It also retrieves the product associated with the price, then uses the product’s name and image to render the payment page.
L93: #### Payment Links
L94: 
L95: Use the Dashboard to create a Payment Link based on a price. The Payment Link uses the price to compute the order total. It also retrieves the product associated with the price. The product’s name and image are used to render the payment page.
L96: #### Subscriptions
L97: 
L98: When creating a Subscription, specify the price `id`. The price must be recurring. The [recurrence interval](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices/object.md#price_object-recurring-interval) for the price defines the subscription’s billing period, and the amount for the price defines how much the subscription charges in each billing period. You can add more than one price to the same subscription as long as they have the same recurrence interval.
L99: #### Quotes
L100: 
L101: When creating a Quote, specify the price `id`. Quotes model the cost of either a one-off invoice or subscription. When a customer accepts the quote, ​​Stripe automatically creates all relevant invoices and subscriptions.
L102: 
L103: #### Invoices
L104: 
L105: When creating an invoice, specify the price `id` for each line item. The invoice uses the price to compute the invoice total. It also retrieves the product associated with the price and uses `product.name` when rendering the invoice as a web page or PDF.
L106: ## Manage existing products and prices
L107: 
L108: You can update product details through the Dashboard or API. For example, you might change the description of a product, or add new product images to use on the [Checkout](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout.md) page.
L109: If you’re no longer selling a product, you can archive both it and the price through the Dashboard by clicking the **Archive** button, or through the API by setting `active` to `false`. We store the archived product and price information indefinitely to maintain records of past transactions.
L110: In general, you can’t delete products or prices, you can only archive them. In certain cases, you can use the Dashboard to delete a price that has never been used, or to delete a product that doesn’t have any prices set.
L111: To change the price of a product, create a new price for the new amount, then archive the existing price by setting `active` to `false`. Instead of changing the `unit_amount` on the existing price, you need to create a new price to make sure that we keep the existing price as an immutable record of past transactions.
L112: You can set a [default price](https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/manage-prices.md#default-price) on a product to specify the most common price to present to customers. You can change the default price to another price later, such as if you increase the price of your product.
L113: ## Understand product and price compatibility
L114: 
L115: Not all features of products and prices are compatible with all Stripe APIs. Consult the following table for compatibility information.
L116: | Feature | Checkout | Payment Links | Quotes | Subscriptions | Invoices |
L117: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
L118: | Product images | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | (Ignored*) | (Ignored*) | (Ignored*) |
L119: | Product descriptions | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | (Ignored*) | (Ignored*) |
L120: | Product tax codes | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported |
L121: | Product statement descriptor | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | (Ignored*) | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported |
L122: | Recurring prices | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported |
L123: | Multi-currency prices | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | (Ignored*) | ✓ Supported | (Ignored*) |
L124: | Tiered prices | ✓ Supported | (Disallowed*) | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported |
L125: | Decimal amounts (for example, charging half-a-cent per unit) | ✓ Supported | (Disallowed*) | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported |
L126: | Usage-based prices | ✓ Supported | (Disallowed*) | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported |
L127: | Customer chooses price | ✓ Supported | ✓ Supported | (Disallowed*) | (Disallowed*) | (Disallowed*) |
L128: Entries marked as (Disallowed) indicate that if a product or price uses this feature, you can’t use that product or price with this Stripe API.
L129: 
L130: Entries marked as (Ignored) indicate that the feature has no effect with this Stripe API, but you can still use the product or price as usual.
L131: ## Understand limitations
L132: 
L133: We don’t limit the number of customers, coupons, products, prices, or most other objects that you can create in your Stripe account.
L134: 
L135: When using recurring prices with Subscriptions:
L136: - If you don’t use [flexible billing mode](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/billing-mode.md) to support [mixed interval subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/mixed-interval.md), then all prices on a Subscription must have the same [recurring.interval](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices/create.md#create_price-recurring-interval) and [recurring.interval_count](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices/create.md#create_price-recurring-interval_count)
L137: - The maximum interval time period of a price is 3 years
